newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares rally on back of budget optimism.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares rally on back of budget optimism.

text.p: Indian stocks on Wednesday continued to claw back ground lost in the aftershock of the Congress party's move to oust Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition government, dealers said.
Growing confidence that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's widely acclaimed 1997/98 (April-March) budget will be salvaged from the political mess shone through the gloom, dealers said.
"People expect the budget to be passed, positive statements by political parties have helped firm prices," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Bombay's Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers.

Deve Gowda's crippled 15-party government has to face a trust vote in parliament on April 11 after the Congress party on Sunday withdrew make-or-break support, plunging the country into a political crisis and putting the budget in jeopardy.
But parliament officials said on Wednesday major parties were trying to rescue the budget from the political chaos.
Analysts said the market offered good investment values.

"I would recomend actually buying on the dip right now, because long term and medium term, India does offer very good earnings prospects," Dilip Rathore, senior economist at W.I. Carr, told Reuters Financial Television on Wednesday.
The Congress move chopped 302 points or over eight percent off the Bombay index on Monday, its fourth largest decline ever.
But hopes that parliament would pass the budget regardless of the political crisis helped Bombay shares climb two percent on Tuesday, analysts said.

"The crisis has given a message that there is a political consensus on the reforms and I think that would be the key to the further growth of investment into the country," Tushar Sarda, president and chief executive at Daewoo Securities told Reuters Financial Televison.
